articles.title: Manoj Bajpayee’s ‘Last Man in Tower’ Sets September Indian Release From Rana Daggubati’s Spirit Media, Unveils Teaser (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: “Last Man in Tower,” the Aravind Adiga adaptation starring Manoj Bajpayee, is headed to Indian theaters this September and has unveiled its first teaser. The film, directed by Ben Rekhi and produced by Rana Daggubati’s Spirit Media, will mark the first time Bajpayee and co-star Boman Irani have…
body: The release will also be a milestone for Spirit Media, the Hyderabad-based company “Baahubali” star Daggubati founded in 2005: it is the outfit’s first Hindi feature production.

Daggubati said: “‘Last Man in Tower’ is a deeply human story. What drew us to it was how naturally it finds something universal in the lives of a very specific group of people. There is something very compelling about the way it explores the choices we make and the things we hold on to. The entire ensemble of cast led by Manoj, Divya, and Boman bring an incredible depth to their characters. ‘Last Man in Tower’ also marks an important milestone for Spirit Media as our first Hindi feature production, and our continued effort towards creating space for fresh new stories and voices for the big-screen audience.”

Rekhi is a Los Angeles-based director whose credits include the SXSW Audience Award-winning “Waterborne” and “Watch List,” which earned 11 nominations at the Filipino Oscars and won two. His documentary short “The Breakthrough Group” was qualified for the 2026 Academy Awards in the best documentary short subject category. “Last Man in Tower” is his sixth feature.

articles.title: ‘Who Has Time to Watch All This Crap?’: Inside 10 Anonymous Emmy Ballots as Voting Officially Closes
articles.summary: Emmy voting is now closed, and not a moment too soon. Every year, more than 27,000 members of the Television Academy — actors and editors, showrunners and composers, the people who actually make television — sit down with their ballots and decide who walks away with an Emmy.
body: Every voter was also asked the same four questions off the ballot — their biggest snub, the most overspent FYC campaign, the network or streamer having the best season and the one win that would actually move the business. Their answers close each entry.

In the categories deemed “area awards” — hosted nonfiction and variety series — voters have the opportunity to select multiple nominees by answering a simple question: Does this show deserve an Emmy? Yes or No. Interestingly, not one voter Variety spoke with checked “Yes” for every nominee, and only four of those surveyed selected more than one. That strongly suggests voters aren’t viewing these categories as an opportunity to spread the wealth, but rather as a traditional “may the best show win” competition.
Ballots have been edited for length and, where necessary, to protect identities.
The opinions are their own. They’re contradictory, occasionally indefensible and, at least for the purposes of this article, the only ones that matter.

articles.title: ‘Coyote vs. Acme’ Cast and Crew Held a ‘Funeral Screening’ After the Movie Was Shelved: ‘Was Emotional in So Many Ways’
articles.summary: What do you do when you think your movie will never see the light of day? Have a “funeral screening,” of course. That’s exactly what the team behind “Coyote vs. Acme” did when they feared the live-action-animation hybrid comedy was locked in the Warner Bros. vault for good. Luckily, after WB.
body: Director Dave Green said there were “many, many times” he thought “Coyote vs. Acme” would never come out. Despite his disappointment, he described the mood at the “funeral screening” as “celebratory.”

“You can have a New Orleans funeral, [with] a jazz band walking up the street, just having a celebration,” Green joked. “That screening for us was emotional in so many ways. It was a bit of a party because we were able to share the movie with friends and other filmmakers who had never seen the movie. And I got to share it with Will [Forte] and Lana, who never got to see the final movie. So that moment was so charged and electric, and the room played so hot.”

“Coyote vs. Acme” sees “Looney Tunes” villain Wile E. Coyote take the Acme Corporation to court after being injured countless times from using its gadgets (think rocket-powered skates and anvils). Condor and Will Forte star. Other cast members include John Cena, Tone Bell, Martha Kelly, Luis Guzmán, P.J. Byrne and John Early.

articles.title: Harry Styles Pays Tribute to Dolly Parton, Completely Revamps Setlist at Madison Square Garden Opening Night: Concert Review
articles.summary: Apart from the special show he performed with an orchestra in London, Harry Styles has played basically the same set since his “Together, Together” tour opened in Amsterdam 33 shows and nearly three months ago.
body: It was clear from the show’s opening notes that this one would be different: Styles took the stage to “Dance No More,” replacing the previous opener “Are You Listening Yet?,” and then launched into “Carolina,” a deep from his solo debut, which he hadn’t performed live since that first solo tour. From there, songs that were previously played late in the set were performed early (and vice versa), and mid-set, “The Waiting Game” from his latest album, “Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally.,” got its live debut.

Early in the show, Styles thanked opening act Jamie XX and then took a moment to acknowledge a full-circle moment on this opening night. “I was told a story when I got here today,” he said. “I had the great privilege of playing this building for the first time when I was 18 years old,” he said, referencing One Direction’s debut at the venue in 2012. “There’s a gentleman who’s working here who hwas working here then, who shared with me that when I got out of the car that day, I kissed the floor and said, ‘I’ve made it to Madison Square Garden!’” The crowd erupted in cheers.

articles.title: Judge awards Blake Lively $400,000 in legal fees in Justin Baldoni case
articles.summary: The actor had sought $8m in attorney costs resulting from her protracted legal battle with Baldoni. Blake Lively has been awarded more than $400,000 in attorneys’ fees after her 18-month legal battle with Justin Baldoni.
body: On Wednesday, judge Lewis Liman awarded the actor $363,245.40 in attorneys’ fees and $44,206.35 in costs, figures far lower than the $8m Lively had sought.

In a ruling, the judge found that Lively was entitled to only “reasonable” fees. He found that her lawyers’ billing rates were “not unreasonable” in a case of this complexity, but “the number of hours for which Lively seeks reimbursement is unreasonable.”

Liman added that her documentation was incomplete: “Lively has submitted the declaration of a purported attorney fee expert who has reviewed the billing records Lively has not submitted the invoices themselves.”

In December 2024, Lively accused Baldoni of sexual harassment and fostering a hostile work environment on the set of domestic abuse drama It Ends With Us; the director filed a counter-defamation lawsuit against Lively the following month.

articles.title: Farewell, Dr Frank-N-Furter: why Tim Curry’s Rocky Horror Show will go on
articles.summary: The versatile stage performer will always be remembered for his defining film role in The Rocky Horror Picture Show, which turned him into an icon of 70s underground cinema and proto-punk • Tim Curry, star of The Rocky Horror Picture Show and Stephen King’s It, dies aged 80 • Tim Curry on…
body: Over the past decade, the issues of trans identity and gender fluidity couldn’t have been more contemporary, and Tim Curry was an integral part of what might be called their pre-history in pop culture. He was an icon – though maybe now a dimly remembered icon – of the 70s underground cinema and proto-punk.

Curry was a good-looking actor with a tremendous speaking and singing voice, and a versatile performer – he got Tony nominations for his varied stage work on Broadway as Mozart in Amadeus, Alan Swann in My Favorite Year (the part Peter O’Toole played on screen) and as King Arthur in Monty Python’s Spamalot. But it was his strange destiny to be remembered for one role: at once indelibly prominent and weirdly peripheral. He was the sensational Dr Frank-N-Furter in the thoroughly outrageous Rocky Horror Picture Show (1975), the screen version of the 1973 stage show.

articles.title: Mel Brooks’ 20 favorite films to be screened in LA for 100th birthday
articles.summary: Comedian and director’s picks for American Cinematheque series range from Charlie Chaplin’s City Lights to Taika Waititi’s Jojo Rabbit. Twenty of Mel Brooks ’ favorite films of the past century will be screening this fall in Los Angeles, as part of a film series the 100-year-old comedian and…
body: The American Cinematheque, Los Angeles’ year-round nonprofit film festival, worked with Brooks to put together his favorites list, which starts with Charlie Chaplin’s City Lights, from 1931, and ends with Jojo Rabbit, Taika Waititi’s 2019 dark comedy about a Nazi-era German boy who has Adolf Hitler as his imaginary friend.

“For the first time, Brooks is publicly sharing his favorites, with the series offering unique insight into his knowledge and appreciation of film history spanning the last century,” the American Cinematheque said in its description of the series. The event was organized in honor of Brooks’ 100th birthday, which fell this 28 June.
The series does not include any of Brooks’ most famous films, such as The Producers, Blazing Saddles, Young Frankenstein, Spaceballs or Robin Hood: Men in Tights.

In fact, Brooks’ list of favorites, which ranges from major classics such as Double Indemnity and Psycho to big-budget musicals and niche comedies, includes only one of his own movies, The Twelve Chairs, which was perhaps his “ biggest commercial flop ”, and one he has continued to urge more people to watch.

articles.title: Rocky Horror star Tim Curry dies at 80
articles.summary: Curry was best known for playing the outlandish Frank-N-Furter in cult film The Rocky Horror Picture Show.
body: English actor Tim Curry, best known for playing the outlandish Frank-N-Furter in film musical The Rocky Horror Picture Show, has died at the age of 80.
Curry first played the role on stage before the film version, which was released in 1975 and has remained a cult favourite.
The actor also played fearsome clown Pennywise in the 1990 TV version of Stephen King's It, and was Long John Silver in 1996's Muppet Treasure Island.
His other films included Annie, The Hunt for Red October, Home Alone 2, Scary Movie 2 and he was nominated for three Tony Awards on Broadway.

articles.summary: The comedian interrupted North West Tonight weather presenter Molly Brewer as she gave her report.
body: BBC North West Tonight's Molly Brewer was presenting her report when Kay joined her on screen.
The Bolton comedian's impromptu appearance was reminiscent of when he famously interrupted the late Dianne Oxberry's forecast in 2011, and declared she "made it sunshine for everybody".

It came as Kay was speaking about staging a one-off show at Blackpool's Opera House next month to raise funds for vital heart treatment in the United States for 19-year-old Fin Cormack from Prenton, Merseyside.

articles.title: The Walking Dead Officially Brings Back Its Scariest Villain After Years Away
articles.summary: The Walking Dead: Dead City Season 3 has officially brought back the most terrifying version of Negan as the character grapples with his dark side.
body: Editor's note: The below contains spoilers for The Walking Dead: Dead City Season 3 Episode 5.

When The Walking Dead debuted on AMC in 2010, it was about much more than the fight between the living and the undead, with other humans often as terrifying as any horde of walkers, if not more so. In the early seasons, Rick Grimes ( Andrew Lincoln ) and company battled a host of big bads before encountering the leader of a group called the Saviors, Negan ( Jeffrey Dean Morgan ), whose introduction was so violent and controversial that many fans stopped watching the show and never returned.

Negan, however, wasn't written off. In fact, he's still around in the spin-off The Walking Dead: Dead City, which he leads alongside Maggie ( Lauren Cohan ), the woman whose husband he once killed right in front of her. The series started strong, but faltered after a disappointing second season, largely because Negan became mopey and listless. Thankfully, The Walking Dead: Dead City has rebounded with a great Season 3. I n the latest episode, Negan's attempts to be good crumble, and the terrifying person he used to be is now threatening to make a bigger comeback.
points: The Walking Dead: Dead City Season 3 has officially brought back the most terrifying version of Negan as the character grapples with his dark side.
